findings.checked: Actual uniform-Schmidt and shifted-star witnesses use disjoint physical slots. The paired eight-unit bound is an all-aspect physical input. The middle normalized spectrum has O(1/m) deviations, while the m^2-2 exceptional square mass remains O(1) uniformly in n. The actual second eigenvalue is bounded away from three. Isolating the largest power leaves an exponentially smaller exceptional term and a middle Taylor term; in the sublinear order window its relative error is independent of aspect.

The projection-plus-spike Schmidt SOS expands exactly with nonnegative coefficients. The adaptive integer H=ceil(sqrt(alpha*m)) gives alpha/(H+3)<=sqrt(alpha/m), H/m->0 and alpha/m->0 uniformly, so the actual peak error is o(1/alpha). The exact normalized spectrum and rest-variance expression retain trace normalization and integer rank rounding. Dividing the rest variance by gamma controls its corrections uniformly, matching the sum of the two moment contributions rather than their maximum.

The actual-state power reduction has a uniform additive error after division by u_D^alpha. Relative entropy optimality is first shown to force the top eigenvalue to three, including supercritical chi; only then is the reduction made relative to the actual largest power. The softplus ratio gives h->0 for bounded-above chi and h/chi->0 for chi->infinity, combined by h/(1+chi_+)->0. The moment condition is the stricter h->0. Shifted-star rigidity makes all remaining actual eigenvalues flat and excludes singular near-optimizers.

The least pivot-relative q=t*ell is kept distinct from the actual normalized least eigenvalue. The shifted star controls the rest of the exceptional head and bounds the full smallest paired width by min(1,h_0*q). Multiplying the singular kernel by alpha before comparison gives a bounded endpoint contribution. Exact pivot centering retains D*f_alpha(t-1). Taylor errors are bounded by alpha*(epsilon_m+nu_m)*C and hence are o(1+alpha*gamma), with no lower bound on alpha.

The entropy-log error is uniformly negligible because A_alpha/D=O(D^-1+alpha/m^2), even when alpha*gamma is unbounded. The sharper variance cap is applied before optimization. On q<=1/h_0 the scalar expression is convex, so its maximum is one of the two endpoints; on q>=1/h_0 the best point is 1/h_0. Replacing h_0 by m creates only o(1+alpha*gamma). The target W is comparable to 1+alpha*gamma throughout the range.

The adaptive negative-family integer H tends to infinity uniformly while H/m->0 and alpha*log H->0. Its actual Schmidt SOS is valid and the least eigenvalue is positive. The normalized least power is m^-alpha+o(1) uniformly, while the rest variance divided by gamma tends to one. The singular and full-rank families match both branches without a surrogate-spectrum or existence gap.

At finite tau,c with c>0, gamma diverges and Q/gamma is compact. A limiting least-power value below a=e^-tau forces (m*ell)^alpha below one by a fixed margin; since alpha->0, m*ell->0 and the variance coordinate tends to zero. This yields the stated low/high criteria. At c=2a only (0,0) and (a,1) can saturate; the distance-to-two-points condition permits alternation. The c=0 case uses alpha*Q->0 without incorrectly requiring Q/gamma->0.

For each actual state, Renyi entropy monotonicity follows from convexity of the positive-eigenvalue power log, including the continuous alpha=1 value. The optimized deficit is therefore monotone. A finite order grid and the relative continuity modulus of Phi, uniform over gamma>=1, yield compact-order uniformity from inherited fixed-order uniform-in-n statements. No moving-order uniformity is presumed. Endpoint and compact subsequence arguments prove the stated suprema; unrestricted-aspect alpha comparable to m is not silently inserted.

findings.checked: On compact positive-order intervals the normalized kernel is Lipschitz in order with a bound proportional to x^2, including x=-1 by an integrable endpoint majorant. The actual-state entropy expansion has no artificial pole at alpha=1. Thus moving alpha_j toward a finite alpha_0 changes every scaled state deficit by o(1), and the transition rows inherit the fixed transition theorem rather than a one-sided coercivity estimate. The 1/2<alpha<1 row is proved through a strict positive mixture of the half-order and von Neumann kernel bounds. The alpha->0 and infinity rows use their new endpoint state identities.

For arbitrary aspect and all diverging alpha, the middle factor (1+delta_m)^alpha is kept until division of its logarithm by alpha-1. The pure spike plus Jensen give the lower positive-part bound. The upper error is O(1/m)+O((1+log alpha)/(alpha-1)), uniform in n and alpha>=L_m. The statement is an absolute-error law and does not claim the unresolved first nonzero relative window.
